_doc: The Stock Exchange and the crypto kiosk (core/markets.gd). Prices are a seeded walk per in-game day: drift and vol are per day (log), season adds to the drift by in-game season (spring, summer, autumn, winter; see Markets.season_of), wet is how a wet day (+1) or a dry one (-1) moves it, story shocks apply from the day the player first finds the flag set, badge and rewild shocks per Stone and per rewilding stage. div is the yearly dividend yield, paid a quarter at a time every 30 days. Board 'dublin' lists the euro shares; every other board lists the sterling ones.

companies.name: Pennine Mills
companies.about: Cotton and wool since 1820. The looms are quieter now, but the jumpers are excellent.

companies.name: Mersey Ferries
companies.about: Ferries across the Mersey, and a song about them nobody can get out of their heads.

companies.name: Cornish Tin
companies.about: Tin out of Cornwall since the Bronze Age. Every few years someone swears there's a new seam.

companies.name: Glasgow Shipyards
companies.about: Built on the Clyde. Ships, cranes and an unshakeable belief in the next big order.

companies.name: Welsh Slate
companies.about: Roofs half the world, from the quarries above Llanberis. Grey, dependable, slightly damp.

companies.name: Sanctuary Holdings
companies.about: Runs the Sanctuaries. Steady as a nurse's hands. Shares rise every time something gets rewilded.

companies.name: Vane Industries
companies.about: Lord Vane's empire: heritage experiences, tote bags and a glass tower. Analysts call it visionary. Analysts are paid by Vane.

companies.name: Kettle & Co
companies.about: Builder's tea by the tonne. When it rains, the nation puts the kettle on and Kettle & Co rises with it.

companies.name: Brolly & Sons
companies.about: Umbrellas, made in Manchester, for obvious reasons. Lives and dies by the forecast.

companies.name: Speyside Distillers
companies.about: Single malt from the Spey, aged in oak and patience. Sales do rather well in winter.

companies.name: Golden Vale Creamery
companies.about: Butter from the Golden Vale. Grass-fed cows, rain-fed grass, and a lot of rain.

companies.name: Silicon Quay
companies.about: An app company in the Docklands. Nobody is sure what the app does, including, it's said, the app.

manchester.name: Royal Exchange
manchester.line: Built for cotton, now trading everything. Mind the pigeons in the dome.

london.name: The City
london.line: The Square Mile. Pinstripes, sandwiches and other people's money.

edinburgh.name: Edinburgh Exchange
edinburgh.line: Prudent Scottish finance. The kettle is older than the building.

dublin.name: Dublin Exchange
dublin.line: Euro listings by the Liffey. The coffee is grand.

coin.name: Doggerel
coin.about: A cryptocurrency backed by a very short poem about a dog. The poem does not scan.

up: {name} soars after a very confident press release
{name} up on rumours of a royal visit
{name} climbs as analysts discover the word 'synergy'
{name} rallies; a man on the radio said it would
{name} jumps after a strong quarter and a stronger biscuit tin
down: {name} slides after the chairman is seen on a bus
{name} falls as the auditor asks a follow-up question
{name} dips on a gloomy forecast and a gloomier logo
{name} tumbles after a typo in the annual report
{name} drops; nobody can explain why, least of all {name}
fx_up: Pound perks up as the Bank of England raises an eyebrow
Sterling firms after a surprisingly cheerful budget
Pound strengthens; the tourists in Temple Bar are delighted
fx_down: Pound wobbles after a long lunch at the Treasury
Sterling slips on a damp set of trade figures
Euro gains as Frankfurt sounds very sure of itself
wet: Rain across the isles: umbrellas and tea in demand
Another wet one. Brolly & Sons rubbing its hands
dry: Sunshine forecast: ferry bookings up, brolly sales down
A dry spell. The nation puts its umbrella away, briefly

story.ashcombe1_done: Cornish Tin up on talk of strange digging at Tintagel
story.ashcombe2_done: Geevor fiasco: Cornish Tin sinks, Vane Industries buys the mess
story.kerrigan1_done: Vane Industries opens an Irish office. Nobody asked it to
story.ch7_judged: Vane Industries up after a mysterious Newgrange deal
story.ch8_vane: Vane's Causeway marquee a sell-out. Shares surge
story.strachan2_done: Vane Industries buys a boat for Loch Ness. Investors cheer, the loch does not
story.moot_won: Moot winner crowned; Vane Industries says this is good for business
story.game_complete: VANE INDUSTRIES COLLAPSES as the glass tower empties. Sanctuary Holdings up
story.badge_stone: Welsh Slate rises as Llanberis quarry gets a new Keeper's blessing
story.badge_iron: Glasgow Shipyards up on fresh orders from Belfast
story.badge_kin: Golden Vale Creamery up as Dublin celebrates a new Stone holder
story.visited_dublin: Ferry traffic to Dublin booms. Silicon Quay launches an app about it

coin_moon: {coin} TO THE MOON (says a man in a hoodie)
{coin} doubles after a celebrity posts a dog
{coin} up; the poem has been translated into Welsh
coin_dump: {coin} slumps as the dog in the poem is revealed to be a cat
{coin} down; someone read the white paper
coin_rug: {coin} developers 'pop out for milk', taking the liquidity with them
{coin} is no more. The website now sells garden furniture
quiet: Markets steady. Traders discuss the weather at length
A quiet day in the City. Someone ordered a second sandwich
Little movement. The tea trolley was the day's main event
